introduction: What are angels? ‘Abdu’l-Bahá gives two answers, and holds both. They are “the confirmations of God and His celestial powers,” and they are human souls, here or in the next world, who have become detached and heavenly. With that key the readings open a wide range of scriptural language: guardian angels, Gabriel, Isráfíl and Azrael, the angels who bowed to Adam, the angels round the Throne, the jinn, and the angels who come to welcome a soul at death. Letters of consolation and encouragement use the imagery freely, for a person will be surrounded and helped. The Bible and the Qur’án supply the passages the readings draw on: Jacob’s ladder, the psalms, the Annunciation, the chariots of fire, the Night of Power. Lincoln’s “better angels of our nature” is the best-known modern use of the word for something in ourselves. Luke’s heavenly host stands for the plain sense that angels are beings who can be seen. Paul warns against the worship of angels, the Sadducees denied them, and Pascal and Madison doubt that men can be angels at all.
questions: Angels are God’s confirmations, and angels are sanctified human souls. Reread the shepherds’ night in Luke with each meaning. What does each bring out?
“He shall give his angels charge over thee.” If the guardian angels are “Divine Powers,” what does a person rely on when he asks for protection?
The readings say human beings can become angels. Pascal warns that whoever would act the angel acts the brute. What distinguishes the two?
Those who have died “may be the mediators of God’s power to you.” Paul warns against “worshipping of angels.” How do the Bahá’í writings keep the first from becoming the second?
‘Abdu’l-Bahá calls belief in jinn and devils superstition while keeping angels. On what principle does he interpret one and dismiss the other?
Many of these passages were written to console or encourage a particular person. What does the language of angels do in such a letter that plainer words would not?

outside.why: “The meaning of ‘angels’ is the confirmations of God and His celestial powers.” A psalm had said something close: who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire.
Angels “will come down to their aid.” The Qur’án of the first Muslims’ first battle: I will help you with a thousand of the angels, rank on rank.

Angels are confirmations and powers. Luke tells of something seen and heard over a field at night: suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God. What is kept and what is given up when such scenes are read as ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reads them?
“Spiritual and merciful powers.” The Letter to the Hebrews: are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
“In one sense the angels are those sanctified souls” who are detached from the world. Of Stephen before his judges: all that sat in the council saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes this psalm: he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
Angels are human souls with heavenly attributes, those of whom it was said, “We shall make men after Our likeness.” Genesis: let us make man in our image, after our likeness.
Lincoln used the word of a part of every person: the better angels of our nature.

Human beings may become angels. Pascal distrusted the ambition: man is neither angel nor brute, and the unfortunate thing is that he who would act the angel acts the brute. What is the difference between acquiring heavenly qualities and “acting the angel”?

Those who have gone before “may be the mediators of God’s power to you.” On the mountain the disciples saw two who had died centuries earlier: there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.

Souls on the other side may mediate help, though it is the one Holy Spirit that strengthens. Paul was wary of attention to intermediaries: let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels. Where is the line between asking help through holy souls and what Paul warns against?
“Let the angels of Thy loving-kindness descend successively upon her.” A psalm: the angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him.
The angels of the Kingdom shall surround thee, and “thy tongue shall utter fluently.” Jesus’ promise without the image: I will give you a mouth and wisdom.
Confirmations sent “successively.” Jacob’s dream: a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
If you remain steadfast you will be assisted. Elisha’s servant had his eyes opened: behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.
A dream of angels enclosed in a letter. An angel came to Peter in prison, and he wist not that it was true; but thought he saw a vision.
“Like the hosts of angels, circle round the throne.” ‘Abdu’l-Bahá quotes the Qur’án: thou seest the angels thronging round the Throne, hymning the praises of their Lord.
The same sight in the Book of Revelation: I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne; and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand.
The trustworthy are “remembered by the Concourse on High.” Jesus: there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
“The angels of inspiration … teach thee.” Daniel at prayer: the man Gabriel touched me and said, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding.
The guardian angels are “Divine Powers” without whose protection humanity could not exist a moment. Jesus of children: in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father.
A newspaper whose subscribers are the angels. Malachi: a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord.
Angels “longed to minister.” The First Letter of Peter: which things the angels desire to look into.
Ministering angels come down. In Gethsemane: there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.
The angels address a woman: “God hath chosen thee.” The original of all such greetings ended with her answer: behold the handmaid of the Lord.
In this world there are “the angels of the All-Merciful” who bring glad tidings and guide. The Letter to the Hebrews: some have entertained angels unawares.
The jinn are “imperceptible forces.” The Qur’án’s verse on them: the jinn did He create of smokeless fire.

Jinn and devils as imagined beings are “mere superstition,” and angels are powers and holy souls. The party in Jerusalem that denied such beings outright was not thought orthodox: the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit. How does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s interpretation differ from simple denial?
Isráfíl gives life, as the angel with the trumpet. Paul: the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible.
Azrael, the angel of death. The Qur’án: the angel of death, who hath charge concerning you, will gather you.
“Well-known … for his heartlessness.” Donne spoke back: Death, be not proud, though some have called thee mighty and dreadful, for thou art not so.
The carpet of the Kingdom is spread and the powers of heaven shaken. Jesus: hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.
A vision of angels around a great white throne. Isaiah’s: above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; and one cried unto another, Holy, holy, holy.

God revealed himself “to Christ through the Holy Spirit and to Muḥammad through Gabriel.” Luke has Gabriel earlier, bringing word to Mary: the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee.
“No word doth escape you but that angels from Us are present … as witnesses.” Jesus: every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof.
The Báb recalls the command to the angels. The Qur’án: We told the angels: Fall ye prostrate before Adam! And they fell prostrate, all save Iblís.
And what they said when they heard of man’s creation: wilt Thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we hymn Thy praise?
The pride of Iblís before Adam. The First Letter to Timothy: lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
Isráfíl acts only “by what God sendeth down … by God’s leave.” A psalm: ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.

“I … rely upon God and upon the angels of God.” An angel in Revelation would not let reliance become worship: see thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant. How does the Báb’s prayer order its reliances?
“The angels of the Supreme Assembly pray for thee every morn and eve.” Jesus to Peter: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
The prison is “the place wherefrom ascend and descend the angels.” Jacob, waking from his dream: surely the Lord is in this place; and I knew it not.
“The angels and the Spirit descend at every moment.” The Qur’án of one night: the angels and the Spirit descend therein, by the permission of their Lord. Peace until the rising of the dawn.
Guardian angels stand before the Face and report. The opening scene of Job: there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord.
When noble souls gather and pray, “the inmates of the Concourse on high hearken.” Jesus: where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Do those on the other side see what happens to those they love? “They see all as it affects the spirit.” The Letter to the Hebrews: we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
“The angels of holiness will welcome ye.” The Qur’án: the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised.
The angels welcomed them “with radiant faces.” Horatio over Hamlet: good night sweet prince: and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.
Angels came out to meet a soul. Jesus: the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom.
He sings so as to “enrapture the Concourse on high.” God to Job: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.
Bahá’u’lláh explains “pairs of wings, two, three and four” as diverse stations. The verse: Who appointeth the angels messengers having wings two, three and four.

Angels are of many ranks, and people may join them. James Madison built a constitution on the opposite expectation: if men were angels, no government would be necessary. Which view of human possibility do you find truer to experience, and can both be held?

hebrews-ministering-spirits.text: But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool? Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation

matthew-their-angels-do-always-behold.text: Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven

john-angels-ascending-and-descending.text: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man

acts-sadducees-say-neither-angel-nor-spi.text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both

colossians-worshipping-of-angels.text: Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind

psalm-ye-his-angels-that-excel-in-streng.text: Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word. Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure

psalm-maketh-his-angels-spirits.text: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire

luke-an-angel-strengthening-him.text: And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him

acts-face-of-an-angel.text: And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel

revelation-ten-thousand-times-ten-thousa.text: And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands; Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing

peter-angels-desire-to-look-into.text: Unto whom it was revealed, that not unto themselves, but unto us they did minister the things, which are now reported unto you by them that have preached the gospel unto you with the Holy Ghost sent down from heaven; which things the angels desire to look into

quran-angels-with-wings-two-three-and-fo.text: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who appointeth the angels messengers having wings two, three and four. He multiplieth in creation what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things.

quran-angels-thronging-round-the-throne.text: And thou (O Muhammad) seest the angels thronging round the Throne, hymning the praises of their Lord. And they are judged aright. And it is said: Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds!

quran-angel-of-death-who-hath-charge.text: Say: The angel of death, who hath charge concerning you, will gather you, and afterward unto your Lord ye will be returned.
